chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:

I asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام about a group for whom the sacrificial animals had become expensive, while they were performing tamattuʿ and traveling together. They were not the people of a single household, but rather a company who had gathered together on their journey and whose campsite was one. Could they slaughter a cow? He said: I do not approve of that except in necessity.

key_terms.الْأَضَاحِيُّ: sacrificial animals offered in the context of pilgrimage
key_terms.بَقَرَةً: a cow proposed as a shared sacrificial offering
key_terms.رِفْقَةٌ: a company or group of fellow travelers
key_terms.ضَرُورَةٍ: a state of necessity that permits exception

ai.seo_question: Can unrelated pilgrims performing tamattuʿ share a cow for sacrifice if the cost of offerings is high?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal ruling concerning pilgrims performing tamattuʿ when the cost of sacrificial animals becomes burdensome. It indicates that unrelated companions traveling together should not ordinarily share a cow for their sacrifice, except in a case of necessity.
